High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

втроём.gloss: as three, the three of us

meanings.en: as three, the three of us
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'as three'.

examples.text: Да, теперь мы живём здесь втроём.
examples.trans: Yes, now we live here as three.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'пугать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will scare / frighten'.

examples.text: Неужели ты думал, что меня это испугает?
examples.trans: Did you really think that this would scare me?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и испугать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will scare on time.

meanings.note: Also a flat number in an address. Common feminine noun meaning 'flat, apartment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

examples.text: Неужели президент накажет вас за правду?
examples.trans: Will the president really punish you for the truth?

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

meanings.note: Food, air, news. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').
